pairs.subject: quality-gates
pairs.evidence: lib/kg/provenance.ts:177 guardStampedRows' --allow-unstamped escape is one boolean that waives every provenance problem on every row (a malformed or invented source as well as a missing stamp) and counts them all as 'unstamped', so the hatch is a blanket rather than a waiver naming its finding.

techniques.evidence: lib/kg/provenance.ts:177 One flag silences every problem on every row, not just the absent-stamp finding it is named for. A row with source 'made-up' gets through the same way an unstamped legacy row does, and it is counted as 'unstamped'.

lib/kg/provenance.ts:101 The contract says ref is a DECLARED formula or batch ref, but the check only tests that it is non-empty. A grep found no registry of declared refs anywhere. The 'migration pass ONLY' rule (line 163) is also prose: kg-compute and kg-legislation-ingest accept the flag too.
lib/kg/provenance.ts:23 A declared-inability token: 'unknown' is valid and gets counted on /atlas, so a writer is not pushed into guessing a plausible source.
lib/kg/provenance.ts:91 The refusal names a remedy the writer can apply inside the tree.
lib/kg/provenance.ts:112 The validator runs on the write itself, before the record exists, not on rows read back afterwards.
lib/kg/provenance.test.ts:121 The hand-mirrored copy of the provenance keys in prop-registry.json is asserted equal to the contract, so the two cannot drift apart.
lib/kg/propRegistry.test.ts:25 A seeded typo key proves the detector can go red, and the test asserts it flags only that key.
lib/kg/propRegistry.test.ts:32 A counterexample shows an unknown scope does not quietly turn into 'everything allowed'.
lib/kg/propRegistry.ts:46 The registry is an allowlist, so renaming a key makes it unregistered (flagged) instead of slipping past a denylist.
